_about: Expected values of resources/tools/run_regression.py, one entry per metric: op (>=, <=, ==, >), value,
optional (a metric whose log line does not exist yet is skipped instead of failing) and a free-text note.
Measured by agent AX on 2026-09-26 on the Release build of HEAD a64f9b4 in the clean snapshot worktree
build/agentAX_wt, d3d9 windowed 1280x720. Each note carries the value measured there.
These are REGRESSION bounds, not performance targets. Timings and per-frame counts on this machine vary by a
factor of five with how many agents are building at the same time (the same run measured 20,220 frames idle and
4,380 under load, 2.7 s and 25.2 s of startup), so every load-sensitive bound sits far below its measured value
and exists to catch a counter that went to zero, a crash, or a milestone that stopped being reached - which is
what every defect of waves 4 and 5 actually looked like. Correctness metrics (layout, CoreSmoke, criticals,
physics counts, the walked distance) are load-independent and are pinned tight.
The three optional census metrics are the counters wave 5's packages AR (textures), AS (touches) and AT
(sequence ops) add. The contract is what agent AP's scene census already does: one DISHONORED(bringup) line
reading '<thing> census: <N> ...' whose first integer is the headline count. Flip optional to false once the
line is in HEAD, so the counter can never be dropped again without failing this run.

Agent FM, wave 19, added the newgame and options stages and their ten rows. They are the first two stages that do NOT pass -startmap: they boot the configuration the user plays (-playdefaults turns on the Core/Src/UnMisc.cpp table the shipped executable compiles in) and drive the game's own menu. Their bounds are cliff detectors in the same sense as the rest: newgame_menu_open_seconds >= 10 is what catches a front end that closes its own menu (wave 17's b540be6 closed it after about one second and passed 37/37), and options_alive is the one row written so that a DEAD process FAILS rather than skips - the baseline requires it, so an absent line scores -1.

layout_types.note: xcheck_sdk_layout.py: retail SDK dump types probed

startup_seconds.note: null RHI; 2.7 s measured at HEAD. A cliff detector only: with four other agents building on the same machine the same run measured 25 s, so the bound catches a hang, not a slowdown

d3d9_startup_seconds.note: 3.4 s measured at HEAD (3.2 s in PHASE7.md); cliff detector only, see startup_seconds

d3d9_frames.note: scene rendered, 90 s run: 20,220 measured at HEAD idle, 4,380 under load. The bound says the render loop keeps running, not how fast

d3d9_draws_per_frame.note: static draw-list elements drawn in the busiest census line: 784 at HEAD, 979 in agent AP's run, 588 under load - camera and time dependent. The bound catches the 0 of 6,381 that AP's draw-distance bug produced

d3d9_draw_elements.note: static draw-list elements in the scene; 6,381 in PHASE7.md

d3d9_visible_prims.note: primitives surviving culling in the busiest census line: 392 at HEAD, 279 under load

touch_census.note: agent AS's -distouch census: touch begins. -distouchprobe walks the pawn to each volume, trigger and pickup after -inputtest finishes, because the first map's triggers are 20,000 units from the spawn and a plain walk touches nothing.

inputtest_moved.note: 2D distance the pawn walks; 1029.6 measured at HEAD (1030 in PHASE7.md)

unported_natives.note: distinct natives without a body that actually fire on the walking path. 0 since agent BF ported the attributes system and the fall-damage chain; the bound is what stops one coming back unnoticed.

nullrhi_log_lines.note: guard: 0 means the run never started and no other metric of this stage is trustworthy

d3d9_log_lines.note: guard: 0 means the run never started and no other metric of this stage is trustworthy

inputtest_log_lines.note: guard: 0 means the run never started and no other metric of this stage is trustworthy

probe_natives.note: natives without a body reached only when -distouchprobe walks the pawn to every volume, trigger and pickup: 7 at HEAD. Gameplay a plain walk never reaches, so this is a ratchet to drive down, not a gate.

newgame_log_lines.note: guard: the run reached the menu at all. A boot through the front end logs far more than a -startmap run

newgame_menu_open_seconds.note: last world time at which the front end's own menu movie was still open (-fmmenu). b540be6 would read about 1

newgame_on_mission.note: -fidiag census lines naming l_tower_p: New Game's hub sequence actually committed the map change

newgame_pawns.note: pawns in the opening scene once it lands; agent FI measured 29. The bound catches an empty scene, not a count

options_steps.note: every step of OPTIONS_SCRIPT resolved. A step whose AS2 path stopped existing logs NOT FOUND and is not counted

options_alive.note: world time of the last `fmoptions alive` heartbeat. The user's crash killed the process 0.15 s after the last tab switch, so a dead process cannot reach this

options_as2_errors.note: measured 41 on two consecutive runs with the HUD open and 39 with -nodishud, identical run to run. Tight on purpose: the brief's assertion is that the error count has not RISEN, and a bound with slack in it would not notice a new error class appearing on the Options screen

options_criticals.note: matches `=== Critical error: ===` as well as `Critical: ` - the user's crash log has the first and not the second
